project.name: AskQL
project.description: Fase B — Cross-Source JOINs backend: relationships, loader, context_builder, query_engine, validation

features.name: Cross-Source JOINs Backend
features.description: Support queries combining data from two different sources (GA4+Google Ads, GA4+Meta Ads, etc.)

tasks.title: Create cross-source relationships.yaml
tasks.description: Create schemas/cross_source/relationships.yaml documenting how pairs of sources can be combined. Include GA4↔Google Ads (date-based + UTM), GA4↔Meta Ads (date-based + UTM), Google Ads↔Meta Ads (date-based). Each relationship documents: sources, JOIN strategy, confidence level, required conversions (date format, currency), and example SQL.

hints: Follow same YAML structure as intra-source relationships but add: sources (list of 2), strategy (date_based/utm_based), confidence (high/medium/low), required_conversions (list)
Date formats: GA4 event_date=YYYYMMDD, Google Ads segments_date=YYYY-MM-DD, Meta date_start=YYYY-MM-DD
Currency: Google Ads metrics_cost_micros /1M, Meta spend already in reais
Date-based JOINs are high confidence, UTM-based are medium confidence

acceptance: File schemas/cross_source/relationships.yaml exists and is valid YAML
Contains GA4 <-> Google Ads relationships (date-based and UTM-based)
Contains GA4 <-> Meta Ads relationships (date-based and UTM-based)
Contains Google Ads <-> Meta Ads relationships (date-based only)
Each relationship has: sources, strategy, confidence, required_conversions, example_sql
Example SQL demonstrates correct date alignment and currency normalization

tests.command: python3 -c "import yaml; data=yaml.safe_load(open('schemas/cross_source/relationships.yaml')); assert len(data['relationships']) >= 5; print(f'OK: {len(data["relationships"])} relationships')"

tasks.title: Add load_cross_source_relationships to loader
tasks.description: Add function load_cross_source_relationships(source_a, source_b) to schemas/loader.py that loads cross-source relationships filtered by the given pair of sources. Returns empty list if file doesn't exist. Order of source_a/source_b shouldn't matter (symmetric lookup).

hints: Cross-source file is at schemas/cross_source/relationships.yaml
Filter: return only relationships where {source_a, source_b} matches the 'sources' field
Make lookup symmetric: (ga4, google_ads) == (google_ads, ga4)
Graceful fallback: if file doesn't exist, return []

acceptance: Function load_cross_source_relationships(source_a, source_b) exists in schemas/loader.py
Returns list of relationships filtered by source pair
Symmetric: load_cross_source_relationships('ga4_bigquery', 'google_ads') == load_cross_source_relationships('google_ads', 'ga4_bigquery')
Returns empty list if relationships.yaml doesn't exist
Existing load_schema() and list_sources() still work unchanged

tests.command: python3 -c "from schemas.loader import load_cross_source_relationships, load_schema; r=load_cross_source_relationships('ga4_bigquery','google_ads'); print(f'GA4+GAds: {len(r)} rels'); r2=load_cross_source_relationships('google_ads','ga4_bigquery'); assert len(r)==len(r2), 'Not symmetric'; s=load_schema('google_ads'); assert 'relationships' in s; print('All OK')"

tasks.title: Add multi-source support to context_builder
tasks.description: Extend build_context() to accept optional secondary_source and secondary_dataset. When provided: include schema of both sources, add Cross-Source Relationships section with alignment rules and examples. Keep secondary schema concise (key tables/fields only). When not provided, behavior identical to current.

hints: Add optional params: secondary_source=None, secondary_dataset=None
When secondary_source set: load both schemas, load cross_source relationships
Add new section '## Cross-Source Relationships' after Table Relationships
Include alignment rules: date format conversion, currency normalization
Keep secondary schema concise: only table names + key fields, skip sub_fields
Add _format_cross_source_relationships() helper function
User prompt should mention both sources when cross-source

acceptance: build_context() accepts secondary_source and secondary_dataset optional params
When secondary_source=None, output identical to current (zero regression)
When secondary_source set, prompt includes schemas of both sources
Prompt includes '## Cross-Source Relationships' section with alignment rules
Prompt includes date format conversion rules and currency normalization rules
User prompt mentions both sources when cross-source
Total prompt size < 10k tokens for any cross-source combination

tests.command: python3 -c "from core.context_builder import build_context; ctx1=build_context('google_ads','p','d','test'); assert '## Cross-Source' not in ctx1['system_prompt'], 'Regression'; ctx2=build_context('ga4_bigquery','p','d','test',secondary_source='google_ads',secondary_dataset='d2'); assert '## Cross-Source' in ctx2['system_prompt'], 'Missing cross-source'; print('All OK')"

tasks.title: Add cross-source quality checks
tasks.description: Add two new quality checks: cross_source_date_alignment (verifies date format conversion when combining sources) and cross_source_currency (verifies currency normalization when combining Google Ads micros with Meta Ads reais). Extend run_checks() to accept optional is_cross_source flag.

hints: cross_source_date_alignment: check for PARSE_DATE, FORMAT_DATE, CAST AS DATE, or consistent date format usage
cross_source_currency: if SQL references both cost_micros and spend, check that cost_micros is divided by 1M
Add applies_to: ['cross_source'] — only run when is_cross_source=True
run_checks() gets optional is_cross_source=False param; when True, also runs cross_source checks
Existing 13 checks must not be affected

acceptance: check_cross_source_date_alignment function exists and detects missing date conversion
check_cross_source_currency function exists and detects mixed currency without normalization
Both checks registered in ALL_CHECKS with applies_to=['cross_source']
run_checks() accepts optional is_cross_source param (default False)
When is_cross_source=False, cross_source checks are not run (backward compatible)
When is_cross_source=True, cross_source checks run in addition to source-specific checks
All 13 existing checks still pass (zero regression)

tests.command: python3 -c "from validation.quality_checks import run_checks; r=run_checks('SELECT 1','google_ads'); assert len([c for c in r if 'cross_source' in c['id']])==0, 'Cross-source checks should not run by default'; r2=run_checks('SELECT 1','google_ads',is_cross_source=True); assert len([c for c in r2 if 'cross_source' in c['id']])>=2, 'Cross-source checks missing'; print(f'Default: {len(r)} checks, Cross: {len(r2)} checks — OK')"
